summary: What comes out of the dark when a night at camp in a risky place is interrupted (F16, docs/story/camp.md): by the lie of the land (a town's streets and indoors have their own; elsewhere the region's) and the party's level. Each group is played to the end by the test autopilot at the lowest level it's for, with the party tired as an interrupted night finds it (tests/integration/test_night_visitors.gd), and won exactly as often on seeds 1-8 as the owner set for that level (2026-10-13): 4 of 8 at levels 1-2, 3 at levels 3-5, 2 from level 6.

groups.text: Eyes in the dark beyond the fire, low to the ground, and more of them every time you count.
Something big moves between the trees, then something bigger. The Count's hounds have found your fire.
Shapes walk upright out of the pines, sniffing at the smoke, and the wolves behind them grin.
The reeds part, and the drowned come up out of the water, walking stiffly toward the warmth.
A stink of rot comes off the water ahead of them: ghasts, and the drowned they have been feeding on.
Scarecrows stand at the edge of the firelight that weren't there when you lay down. Behind them, something in a drowned bride's veil begins to wail.
Grey wolves come down from the rocks above the camp, quiet as the snow.
Men in furs come down the slope at a run, axes high, howling like wolves.
A werewolf leads them down off the heights: wild men in furs, and wolves the size of ponies.
The sky over the camp fills with wings, and the dead climb up out of the dark after them.
Bats first, a cloud of them, and then the castle's dead and the things that eat them, crawling toward the warmth.
Pale figures walk out of the dark behind the bats, smiling, in no hurry at all.
Soft footsteps in the empty street. Cutthroats, come to see what strangers carry, and sure that no door will open however loud it gets.
The churchyard gate stands open. The dead come up the street toward the fire, slow and sure, and every shutter stays shut.
Two pale figures walk down the middle of the street, smiling, and the Count's wolves follow at their heels like dogs.
Scratching in the walls, then squeaking, then rats pour out of every crack and gap toward the warmth.
The shadows in the corners don't move when the fire does. Then they peel off the walls, and the dead come through the door behind them.
The fire gutters and burns blue. Something cold comes through the wall, and the dead it has made come with it.
